_comment: Citations for 10e weapon keywords and unit-level core mechanics implemented in code/units.py and code/simulator.py. Sources are Wahapedia core rules and faction pages. Effects marked '(approximation)' note where the SwegHammer model is lossy vs the canonical rule.

weapon.heavy.quoted_text: Each time an attack is made with such a weapon, if the attacking model's unit Remained Stationary this turn, add 1 to that attack's Hit roll.
weapon.heavy.trigger: attacker did not move during this round's movement sub-phase
weapon.heavy.effect: +1 to the Hit roll for this weapon

weapon.assault.quoted_text: If a unit that Advanced this turn contains any models equipped with Assault weapons, it is still eligible to shoot in this turn's Shooting phase.
weapon.assault.trigger: attacker Advanced this round and has at least one Assault weapon
weapon.assault.effect: permitted to shoot this round even though the unit Advanced

weapon.rapid_fire.quoted_text: Each time such a weapon targets a unit within half that weapon's range, the Attacks characteristic of that weapon is increased by the amount denoted by 'x'.
weapon.rapid_fire.trigger: target is within half the weapon's range
weapon.rapid_fire.effect: +X to the Attacks characteristic for this firing

weapon.melta.quoted_text: Each time an attack made with such a weapon targets a unit within half that weapon's range, that attack's Damage characteristic is increased by the amount denoted by 'x'.
weapon.melta.trigger: target is within half the weapon's range
weapon.melta.effect: +X to the Damage characteristic per shot for this firing

weapon.anti_x.quoted_text: Each time an attack is made with such a weapon against a target with the keyword after the word 'Anti-', an unmodified Wound roll of 'x+' scores a Critical Wound.
weapon.anti_x.trigger: target has the keyword named after Anti- (INFANTRY, VEHICLE, etc.)
weapon.anti_x.effect: an unmodified Wound roll of X+ auto-succeeds AND counts as a Critical Wound (10e core: a Critical Wound is by definition a successful Wound roll). Stacks with [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] to bypass saves on the crit.

weapon.lance.quoted_text: Each time an attack is made with such a weapon, if the bearer made a Charge move this turn, add 1 to that attack's Wound roll.
weapon.lance.trigger: attacker declared and completed a successful Charge this round; melee attack
weapon.lance.effect: +1 to the Wound roll for this weapon

weapon.precision.quoted_text: Each time an attack made with such a weapon successfully wounds an Attached unit, if a CHARACTER model in that unit is visible to the attacking model, the attacking model's player can choose to have that attack allocated to that CHARACTER model instead of following the normal attack sequence.
weapon.precision.trigger: ranged attack with PRECISION; target has CHARACTER keyword
weapon.precision.effect: (approximation) cover save bonus does not apply when shooting a CHARACTER target. SwegHammer does not model Attached-unit wound allocation, so we substitute a cover-bypass effect that has roughly the same expected damage gain against bodyguarded characters.

simulator.precision_keyword.quoted_text: Each time an attack made with such a weapon successfully wounds an Attached unit, if a CHARACTER model in that unit is visible to the attacking model, the attacking model's player can choose to have that attack allocated to that CHARACTER model instead of following the normal attack sequence.
simulator.precision_keyword.trigger: attacker carries a PRECISION ranged weapon; target is a non-MONSTER/non-VEHICLE CHARACTER otherwise shielded by Look Out Sir bodyguards beyond 12"
simulator.precision_keyword.effect: the Look Out Sir bodyguard gate in code.army.can_target_for_ranged is bypassed, permitting the shot at the CHARACTER directly. Equivalent of the real rule's wound-allocation override, collapsed onto the simulator's targeting gate because characters are modelled as standalone units and there is no attached-unit wound-allocation step. Lone Operative is NOT bypassed.

weapon.pistol.quoted_text: If a unit contains any models equipped with Pistols, that unit is eligible to shoot in its controlling player's Shooting phase even while it is within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units. In such circumstances, models in that unit equipped with Pistols can only target enemy units that their unit is within Engagement Range of, and can only resolve attacks using their Pistols.
weapon.pistol.trigger: attacker is within Engagement Range (1") of an enemy
weapon.pistol.effect: (approximation) Pistols may fire while in engagement. SwegHammer does not restrict the Pistol shot to only target the engaging enemy or to forbid simultaneous non-Pistol firing; we just allow the activation to proceed instead of being blocked.

weapon.indirect_fire.quoted_text: Weapons with [INDIRECT FIRE] in their profile are known as Indirect Fire weapons, and attacks can be made with them even if the target is not visible to the attacking model. Each time a ranged attack is made with such a weapon against a unit that is not visible to the attacking model, subtract 1 from the Hit roll, the target has the Benefit of Cover against that attack, and an unmodified Hit roll of 1-3 always fails.
weapon.indirect_fire.trigger: ranged attack with INDIRECT FIRE; target is not visible
weapon.indirect_fire.effect: (approximation) Indirect Fire can target units it cannot see, at -1 to Hit. SwegHammer skips line-of-sight when picking the target and applies -1 to Hit when LoS is blocked, but does not grant the target Benefit of Cover or apply the auto-fail on rolls of 1-3.

weapon.one_shot.quoted_text: A weapon with [ONE SHOT] can only be shot once per battle.
weapon.one_shot.trigger: the weapon is selected to shoot
weapon.one_shot.effect: the weapon may only be fired once per battle; subsequent activations skip shooting with it

weapon.torrent.quoted_text: Each time an attack is made with such a weapon, that attack automatically hits the target.
weapon.torrent.effect: skips the to-hit roll, the attack auto-hits (no Critical Hit generated)

weapon.lethal_hits.quoted_text: Each time an attack is made with such a weapon, a Critical Hit automatically wounds the target.
weapon.lethal_hits.trigger: unmodified hit roll of 6 with a LETHAL HITS weapon
weapon.lethal_hits.effect: that Critical Hit auto-wounds (skip the Wound roll); the wound is treated as a normal (non-crit) wound for Devastating Wounds purposes

weapon.sustained_hits.quoted_text: Each time an attack is made with such a weapon, if a Critical Hit is rolled, that attack scores a number of additional hits on the target as denoted by 'x'.
weapon.sustained_hits.trigger: unmodified hit roll of 6 with a SUSTAINED HITS weapon
weapon.sustained_hits.effect: the Critical Hit generates X additional normal hits in addition to the original one

weapon.devastating_wounds.quoted_text: Each time an attack is made with such a weapon, if that attack scores a Critical Wound, no saving throw of any kind can be made against that attack (including invulnerable saving throws).
weapon.devastating_wounds.trigger: unmodified wound roll of 6 (or Anti-keyword crit threshold) with a DEVASTATING WOUNDS weapon
weapon.devastating_wounds.effect: the wound bypasses armour, cover, and invulnerable saves; damage is applied directly

weapon.twin_linked.quoted_text: Each time an attack is made with such a weapon, you can re-roll that attack's Wound roll.
weapon.twin_linked.trigger: any wound roll with a TWIN-LINKED weapon
weapon.twin_linked.effect: (approximation) re-roll a failed Wound roll once. The canonical rule allows re-rolling any wound roll (including a success) - we only re-roll failures, which is the optimal play but marginally less general.

weapon.ignores_cover.quoted_text: Each time an attack is made with such a weapon, the target cannot have the Benefit of Cover against that attack.
weapon.ignores_cover.trigger: any ranged attack with IGNORES COVER
weapon.ignores_cover.effect: target loses the cover save bonus and the heavy-cover -1-to-hit modifier for this attack

weapon.blast.quoted_text: Each time you determine how many attacks are made with a Blast weapon, add 1 to the result for every five models that were in the target unit when you selected it as the target (rounding down).
weapon.blast.trigger: ranged attack with BLAST against a multi-model unit
weapon.blast.effect: (approximation) +1 attack per 5 enemy models in the target unit. SwegHammer counts models in the target's army with the same profile name as a proxy for squad size; it cannot also enforce the canonical 'BLAST may not target units in engagement range' restriction.

weapon.hazardous.quoted_text: After a unit attacks with one or more Hazardous weapons, that unit must take one Hazardous test for each such weapon used. To do so, roll one D6: on a 1, that test is failed and that unit suffers 3 mortal wounds, and if possible those mortal wounds must be allocated to a model equipped with a Hazardous weapon.
weapon.hazardous.trigger: any unit fires or fights with a HAZARDOUS weapon
weapon.hazardous.effect: (approximation) after firing, roll one D6; on a 1 the unit takes 3 mortal wounds. SwegHammer rolls a single test per attacker per activation rather than one per Hazardous weapon used, and bypasses the 'allocate to a model with the weapon' clause because squads are modelled as single Unit instances.

unit.stealth.quoted_text: If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack's Hit roll.
unit.stealth.trigger: target unit has Stealth and is being shot at
unit.stealth.effect: -1 to the attacker's Hit roll (only ranged attacks; melee is unaffected)

unit.fnp.quoted_text: Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by 'x', that wound is ignored and is not lost.
unit.fnp.trigger: model with Feel No Pain takes an unsaved wound or mortal wound
unit.fnp.effect: (approximation) roll one D6 per point of damage; on X+ that wound is ignored. SwegHammer rounds incoming damage to an integer for the dice loop and preserves the fractional remainder un-FNP'd - close enough at expected-value scale but not strictly per-wound.

simulator.cover_light.quoted_text: Until the end of the phase, each time a ranged attack is allocated to a model in this unit while it is receiving the Benefit of Cover, add 1 to the armour saving throw made against that attack. If a model has a Save characteristic of 3+ or better, that model cannot have the Benefit of Cover against attacks made with weapons that have an Armour Penetration characteristic of 0.
simulator.cover_light.trigger: target model stands in LIGHT_COVER terrain (LIGHT_COVER, HEAVY_COVER and RUIN are all equivalent in 10e - each grants the same single Benefit of Cover)
simulator.cover_light.effect: +1 to the armour save (the single-pip Benefit of Cover; universal 2+ floor applies). The AP0 / 3+-save exception is now enforced for ALL models: a target whose base Save is 3+ or better gets no cover against an AP0 attack. Implemented in code.units.Unit.attack (cover_blocked_by_ap0_exception gate).

simulator.cover_heavy.quoted_text: Until the end of the phase, each time a ranged attack is allocated to a model in this unit while it is receiving the Benefit of Cover, add 1 to the armour saving throw made against that attack.
simulator.cover_heavy.trigger: target stands in HEAVY_COVER or RUIN terrain and the attack is ranged
simulator.cover_heavy.effect: +1 to the armour save - the SAME single Benefit of Cover as LIGHT_COVER. There is no terrain -1-to-hit in current 10e (the stale 9th-edition Heavy-Cover / Dense-Cover -1-to-hit was removed): HEAVY_COVER and RUIN no longer differ from LIGHT_COVER for the combat effect. The in_heavy_cover flag is still toggled by Battle._do_shoot but no longer changes the Hit roll.

simulator.masters_of_camouflage.rule_name: Masters of Camouflage (Astra Militarum Recon Element detachment rule)
simulator.masters_of_camouflage.quoted_text: Astra Militarum Walker and Regiment models from your army have the Benefit of Cover.
simulator.masters_of_camouflage.trigger: a ranged attack targets an Astra Militarum INFANTRY or WALKER model while the Recon Element detachment rule is active (gated SWEG_AM_RECON, default-off)
simulator.masters_of_camouflage.effect: the target receives the Benefit of Cover (+1 to its armour save versus ranged attacks; the AP0 / 3+-save exception and the universal 2+ floor still apply). APPROXIMATION: 'Regiment' is not a BSData v10.6.0 keyword (the same gap Born Soldiers proxies), so the gate fires on Astra Militarum INFANTRY or WALKER models; the big VEHICLE tanks are excluded (conservative) and the in-cover stacking-to-3+ half is not modelled (the engine caps cover at a single +1 pip). Implemented in code.units.Unit.attack.

simulator.deep_strike.quoted_text: During deployment, you can set up this unit in Deep Strike Reserves instead of on the battlefield. If you do, then in the Reinforcements step of one of your subsequent Movement phases, you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9" horizontally away from all enemy models. Any Reserves units that have not been set up on the battlefield when the battle ends count as having been destroyed.
simulator.deep_strike.trigger: unit profile has deep_strike=True; battle round >= 2
simulator.deep_strike.effect: (approximation) unit starts in Reserves; arrives from Round 2 onward, placed more than 9" from all enemy models. SwegHammer rolls a 66% chance to arrive each round from Round 2 and force-arrives by Round 4, instead of the canonical 'arrive any subsequent round, destroyed if not on by end of battle'. The unit also counts as having moved on arrival.

simulator.scout.quoted_text: Some models have 'Scouts X"' listed in the abilities section of their datasheet. Before the first turn begins, if every model in a unit has this ability, that unit can make a Normal move of up to X". A unit cannot end this move within 9" horizontally of any enemy models.
simulator.scout.trigger: unit profile has scout_distance > 0; pre-game (before Round 1)
simulator.scout.effect: before the first round, the unit makes a Normal move up to scout_distance inches; the move is the rule, the destination is the AI's tactical choice. Default: toward the nearest enemy (legacy). With SWEG_SCOUT_AI=1 the destination is classified by ROLE (v2): (a) melee-oriented scouts pressure forward toward the nearest enemy; (b) long-range shooty scouts (range >= 24 inches) hold their firing position; (c) short-range / fragile shooty scouts move toward the nearest forward-but-safe contestable objective (no further than ~3 inches past the midline), never into a strictly worse position, else hold. This is an AI heuristic on a real move, like simulator.intelligent_deployment, not a rule change. SwegHammer does not enforce the 'cannot end within 9" of an enemy' clause precisely - it just clamps movement and trusts the deployment distance.

simulator.infiltrators.quoted_text: Some models have 'Infiltrators' listed in the abilities section of their datasheet. During deployment, when you set up a unit with this ability, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9" horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.
simulator.infiltrators.trigger: unit profile has infiltrator=True; during deployment
simulator.infiltrators.effect: (approximation) the unit deploys forward of its standard deployment line, roughly halfway between its own line and the centreline. SwegHammer does not measure 9" from the enemy deployment zone - it just picks a forward line and trusts the geometry.

simulator.reanimation_protocols.quoted_text: If your Army Faction is NECRONS, at the end of your Command phase, each unit from your army with this ability that is on the battlefield activates its Reanimation Protocols and reanimates D3 wounds. … If that unit contains one or more models with fewer than their starting number of wounds remaining, select one of those models; that model regains one lost wound. If all models in that unit have their starting number of wounds, but that unit is not at its Starting Strength, one destroyed model is returned to that unit with one wound remaining.
simulator.reanimation_protocols.trigger: end of round for a Necron army with Reanimation Protocols on a unit that (a) still has at least one alive model and (b) had at least one model destroyed THIS round
simulator.reanimation_protocols.effect: (approximation) per profile per round: if the squad lost at least one model this round, revive 1 destroyed model WITH ONE WOUND REMAINING anchored on a living peer. Fix F-NEC-2 (iter 14): revival no longer restores the model to its FULL wound pool — per the verbatim army-rule allocation, a returned model has 'one wound remaining'. For W1 Warriors / Immortals this is unchanged; for multi-wound NECRONS units (Wraiths W3, Lychguard W2/W3, Praetorians W2, Skorpekh Destroyers W3, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers W3) the previous full-HP behaviour was strictly over-generous. Round-start snapshot vs alive-now gates the 'lost a model this round' clause (Fix F-NEC-1, iter 2 — without this, squads kept reviving every round just because they were below STARTING strength, granting infinite endurance). Cap of 1 per profile per round is a deliberate UNDER-fire vs the codex 'D3 wounds per unit per Command phase' wording (median 2 wounds spent lost-wounds-first then revival) — kept conservative pending the full per-unit wound-budget rewrite. End-of-round timing rather than start-of-Command-phase. Once a profile is completely wiped, reanimation stops (matches canonical 'still on battlefield' constraint).

simulator.sticky_objective.quoted_text: That objective marker remains under your control even if you have no models within range of it, until your opponent controls it at the start or end of any turn.
simulator.sticky_objective.trigger: a sticky_objective unit currently controls an objective (more OC than the enemy within control range)
simulator.sticky_objective.effect: (approximation) once the unit claims the objective, ownership persists across rounds in self._sticky_owner until the opposing side outscores us on it. SwegHammer applies this as a profile-level flag rather than a per-Stratagem opt-in - the 'sticky' status is permanent for any unit with the flag, not single-use.

simulator.objective_control_strictly_gre.quoted_text: A player's Level of Control over an objective marker is equal to the sum of the Objective Control characteristics of all of that player's models within range of that objective marker. The player with the greater Level of Control over the objective marker controls it.
simulator.objective_control_strictly_gre.trigger: any phase-end objective control check (scoring or sticky-claim promotion)
simulator.objective_control_strictly_gre.effect: control of an objective requires strictly greater OC than the opponent; ties yield no controller and therefore cannot trigger sticky-objective promotion (e.g. VIRULENT_VECTORIUM.worldblight_sticky_dg_objectives or any other sticky_objective profile flag). Previously SwegHammer accepted OC ties for sticky promotion (>=), which let Worldblight DG claim sticky on contested markers — corrected to strict > to match Wahapedia's 'greater Level of Control' wording.

simulator.objective_control_base_range.quoted_text: When measuring the distance between models, measure between the closest points of the bases of the models you're measuring to and from.
simulator.objective_control_base_range.trigger: the Objective Control contest checks whether a model is within an objective marker's control range, while no-overlap collision (SWEG_COLLISION) is active
simulator.objective_control_base_range.effect: a model is within range of an objective marker when the CLOSEST POINT of its base is within the control radius, i.e. centre-distance - base_radius <= control_radius (base_radius from code.simulator._bc_model_radius_in). The collision-OFF baseline keeps the centre-only approximation (centre within control_radius) so the OFF path is byte-identical; the base-edge measure is gated SWEG_COLLISION because the artifact it corrects only arises under no-overlap collision — a large base (e.g. a 170mm Imperial Knight) physically pushes enemy model CENTRES past 3" of a marker it stands on, which under the centre-only check would unfaithfully evict base-to-base contesters whose base edge is still within range. Applied in _assign_army_oc. Symmetric across all models and factions (it widens every model's reach by its own base radius); not a per-faction knob.

simulator.collision_friendly_passthrough.rule_name: Making a Move — moving through models
simulator.collision_friendly_passthrough.quoted_text: It can be moved through friendly models, but it cannot end its move on top of another model.
simulator.collision_friendly_passthrough.trigger: a model resolves a move (_move_toward) while no-overlap collision (SWEG_COLLISION) is active
simulator.collision_friendly_passthrough.effect: Under no-overlap collision the mover's PATH is blocked only by ENEMY bases — a non-FLY model 'cannot move through an enemy model' (same Move Units section: 'no part of its base can be moved through an enemy model'), so code.simulator._enemy_path_cap_t stops it at the enemy's near boundary (faithful screening — a Knight cannot pass through an enemy horde). FRIENDLY models are passed through: they never cap the path; only the END is constrained by _collision_pos_legal (no overlap with any model, and a non-FLY model may not end within 1" Engagement Range of an enemy). FLY moves over enemy models (path uncapped) but still may not end on a model or within Engagement Range. This replaces the prior friend-blind bisection walk-back that halted a mover at the near edge of the FIRST blocker (friend or foe), which self-jammed armies — notably clustered Imperial Knight bases — behind their own models. Gated SWEG_COLLISION; the OFF path (occupants is None) is byte-identical. Symmetric across all factions; not a per-faction knob and not a make-way (no other model is moved aside).

simulator.battle_focus.quoted_text: If your Army Faction is ASURYANI, at the start of the battle round, you receive a number of Battle Focus tokens based on the battle size, as shown in the table below. [Incursion: 2 tokens | Strike Force: 4 tokens | Onslaught: 6 tokens]. Each time one of the triggers shown in the Agile Manoeuvres section below occurs, you can spend one Battle Focus token to enable the relevant eligible unit to perform that Agile Manoeuvre. A unit is eligible to perform an Agile Manoeuvre if it has this ability and has not already performed an Agile Manoeuvre in the same phase. Unless otherwise stated, you cannot trigger the same Agile Manoeuvre more than once per phase. At the end of the battle round, all unspent Battle Focus tokens are lost. Star Engines: when an ASURYANI VEHICLE unit from your army Advances, you can spend one Battle Focus token; until the end of that turn, ranged weapons equipped by models in that unit have the [ASSAULT] ability.
simulator.battle_focus.trigger: start of each battle round, for any army containing at least one ASURYANI unit. Battle size derived from army.starting_points: ≤1000 pts = Incursion (2 tokens/round), ≤2000 pts = Strike Force (4 tokens/round, evaluation default), >2000 pts = Onslaught (6 tokens/round). A Battle Focus token is spent when an ASURYANI VEHICLE unit Advanced this round. The codex is explicit that unspent tokens are LOST at the end of the battle round (verbatim quote above) — this is a round-scoped resource, not a carryover pool.
simulator.battle_focus.effect: (approximation) tokens are granted at the start of each battle round via Battle._grant_battle_focus_tokens; spending one lets an Advanced ASURYANI VEHICLE unit shoot anyway, as if its weapons had [ASSAULT] — modelling the Star Engines Agile Manoeuvre only. Gate requires both ASURYANI and VEHICLE keywords per the real rule wording. The other five named Agile Manoeuvres (Swift as the Wind, Flitting Shadows, Sudden Strike, Opportunity Seized, Fade Back) are not modelled. AELDARI-BATTLE-FOCUS-V1 (wave 59): fixed the gate from ASURYANI-only to ASURYANI+VEHICLE. AELDARI-BATTLE-FOCUS-V2 (wave 235): moved from a once-at-battle-start flat pool to a per-round grant scaled by battle size per the verbatim Wahapedia table; Warhost Martial Grace now also adds +1 per round rather than +1 to the starting pool. CORRECTION + fix (gate SWEG_AELDARI_BF_DISCARD, default OFF): the AELDARI-BATTLE-FOCUS-V2 comment previously (incorrectly) claimed the rule text does not say unspent tokens are discarded — it does, verbatim ('At the end of the battle round, all unspent Battle Focus tokens are lost'), which this citation update corrects. Default (gate OFF, legacy, current production default): the grant at `Battle._grant_battle_focus_tokens` is additive (`army.battle_focus_tokens += base_tokens`) and never zeroed, so the pool carries over round to round — a KNOWN divergence from the codex being left in place as the default pending screening. Gate ON: `Battle._run_round` zeroes each army's `battle_focus_tokens` to 0 at the end of every round (after all of that round's Star Engines spends), before the next round's grant, so the pool is round-scoped as the rule requires. Byte-identical off.

simulator.battleshock.quoted_text: If a unit is Below Half-Strength, you must take a Battle-shock test for it. To do so, roll 2D6: if the result equals or exceeds the unit's Leadership characteristic, that test is passed. Otherwise, that test is failed and that unit is Battle-shocked until the start of your next Command phase. While a unit is Battle-shocked, the Objective Control characteristic of all of its models is 0, you cannot use Stratagems to affect that unit, and that unit must take Desperate Escape tests if it Falls Back.
simulator.battleshock.trigger: start of own Command phase (Round 1 onward); unit is Below Half-Strength
simulator.battleshock.effect: (approximation) the unit rolls 2D6; fail (< Ld) drops its OC to 0 for objective scoring this round AND the unit is removed from the candidate pool of friend/enemy stratagem target pickers (`_highest_dpa_unit`, `_most_vulnerable_unit`, `_highest_threat_enemy`) so detachment stratagems cannot select it as their subject for the round. SwegHammer ignores the 'Desperate Escape on Fall Back' consequence because Fall Back desperate escape is otherwise handled by the dedicated Fall Back gate (#171). Detachment ld_bonus / enemy_ld_penalty compose into the test target. Task #168 moved the test to run BEFORE the round-start stratagem dispatcher so the lockout is observable when the dispatcher picks targets.

simulator.insane_bravery.quoted_text: INSANE BRAVERY 1CP. Epic Deed Stratagem. WHEN: Battle-shock step of your Command phase, just before you take a Battle-shock test for a unit from your army. TARGET: That unit from your army. EFFECT: Your unit automatically passes that Battle-shock test. RESTRICTIONS: You cannot use this Stratagem more than once per battle.
simulator.insane_bravery.trigger: Battle-shock step of own Command phase, just before a friendly unit takes a Battle-shock test (the simulator fires it only when the unit would otherwise FAIL and is contesting an objective)
simulator.insane_bravery.effect: (approximation) the owning army spends 1 Command Point to auto-pass a would-be-failed Battle-shock test, at most once per battle (`self._insane_bravery_used`), CP-gated (`army.command_points >= 1`), and only when the squad is within an objective's control radius (`self._squad_on_objective`) — the heuristic for when a real player burns it (to keep an objective-contesting unit's Objective Control, which Battle-shock would drop to 0). Modelled by forcing the 2D6 roll up to the test target so the existing pass branches resolve it as a pass. Even-handed across all factions. Gated SWEG_INSANE (default ON; =0 disables for the isolation A/B).

simulator.mob_rule.quoted_text: Each time a Battle-shock test is taken for an ORKS unit from your army, if that unit has 10 or more models in it, that test is automatically passed.
simulator.mob_rule.trigger: Battle-shock test for an Orks unit; that unit (squad) currently has 10+ alive models
simulator.mob_rule.effect: the unit auto-passes its Battle-shock test (no 2D6 roll). SwegHammer models each squad member as a separate Unit instance; the canonical '10+ models in the unit' is approximated as '10+ alive Ork models sharing the same datasheet name'. Big Boyz / Gretchin / Beast Snagga / Kommandos blocks (typically 10-30 strong) auto-pass; small squads (Tankbustas 6, Meganobz 2, Killa Kans 3) and lone characters / vehicles do not. Prior implementation (pre-ORKS-DIAG) gated on army-wide 10+ which gave Mob Rule to every Ork unit whenever any single big mob was alive — fixed to per-squad on 2026-05-23.

simulator.waaagh.quoted_text: Once per battle, in your Command phase, you can declare a WAAAGH! is in effect for that turn. While a WAAAGH! is in effect for your turn: In your Movement phase, each unit in your army that has the WAAAGH! ability is eligible to declare a charge in that phase even if it Advanced in your Movement phase. Add 1 to Charge rolls made for units in your army. Add 1 to the Wound rolls for melee attacks made by models in your army. Each model in your army has a 5+ invulnerable save against melee attacks.
simulator.waaagh.trigger: Command phase of an Orks army; WAAAGH! has not yet been declared this battle; AI decides this is the round (first-charge trigger: ≥1 Ork unit wants_to_charge AND has a chargeable target within 12" AND Boyz at ≥40% of starting count; emergency Round 2+ if below 70% starting points; Round 4 fallback if first-charge trigger never fired; Round 5 force-fire)
simulator.waaagh.effect: (approximation) the army marks `waaagh_round_unlocked = current_round`; on that turn only, Ork attackers (a) add +1 to the melee Wound roll and (b) add +1 to the 2D6 Charge roll. APPROXIMATION: the army-wide 5+ invulnerable save vs melee attacks and the 'Advance counts as Charge' leg are still NOT modelled — deferred to future iterations.

simulator.markerlights.quoted_text: Each time a T'AU EMPIRE unit from your army (excluding KROOT units) is selected to shoot, ranged weapons equipped by models in your unit have their Ballistic Skill characteristic improved by 1 and have the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability while targeting an enemy unit that is visible to one or more friendly MARKERLIGHT units that are not within Engagement Range of one or more enemy models.
simulator.markerlights.trigger: a T'au Empire (non-KROOT) unit shoots an enemy that is a Guided/Marked target — i.e. visible to a friendly alive MARKERLIGHT-keyword unit. Marked status is populated each round by Battle._run_markerlight_phase (each alive MARKERLIGHT carrier marks the highest-points enemy within 36" + line of sight).
simulator.markerlights.effect: the base army-rule buff: a T'au Empire ranged attacker firing at a Guided target gets +1 to the Hit roll (Ballistic Skill improved by 1, applied via `hit_mod_delta` under the 10e +/-1 cap) AND [SUSTAINED HITS 1] (applied via `effective_sustained_hits`), in EVERY detachment and EVERY round. This is distinct from and STACKS WITH the Mont'ka Killing Blow [LETHAL HITS]-on-Guided detachment effect (rounds 1-3 only). T-AU-MARKERLIGHT-BASE (2026-06-03): the base +1 BS + [SUSTAINED HITS 1] was previously UNMODELLED — `Army.guided_enemy_uids` was populated each round but only the Mont'ka [LETHAL HITS] consumer read it; this entry now applies the army-rule base buff. APPROXIMATION: the sim marks the single highest-points enemy per MARKERLIGHT carrier (a conservative under-approximation of the verbatim 'any target visible to a Markerlight unit'); tokens persist for the round and clear at end-of-round.

simulator.markerlight_emission.quoted_text: MARKERLIGHT: Each time a unit from your army shoots, after that unit has resolved its attacks, you can select one enemy unit that was targeted by one or more attacks made with a weapon equipped with this ability this phase and that had one or more of those attacks score a hit. That enemy unit is a Marked unit until the end of the turn. Markerlight has a 36" range and uses the firing model's Ballistic Skill characteristic; targets must be within range and visible (line of sight) and the standard target-eligibility restrictions apply.
simulator.markerlight_emission.trigger: _run_markerlight_phase is iterating MARKERLIGHT-keyword carriers in a T'au army; per carrier, a candidate enemy must (a) lie within 36" of the carrier, (b) be visible via Map.has_line_of_sight, and (c) pass can_target_for_ranged (Look Out Sir / Lone Operative); then a d6 Hit roll is rolled against the carrier's Ballistic Skill (`_prob_to_target(hit_probability)`)
simulator.markerlight_emission.effect: if the candidate is in range AND in line of sight AND a legal target AND the Hit roll succeeds, the target's uid is added to `army.guided_enemy_uids` for the round. On any gate failing or the Hit roll missing, no token is granted by that carrier. This corrects the pre-iter27 behaviour where every MARKERLIGHT-keyword unit auto-Guided a target with no Hit roll / no LoS / no range cap — the previous code was a placeholder pending this iter's rule-faithfulness correction.

simulator.stratagem_per_command_phase_ca.rule_name: Command Point economy (per-Command-phase stratagem cap, AI heuristic)
simulator.stratagem_per_command_phase_ca.quoted_text: Players gain 1CP at the start of their Command phase (a maximum of 15CP can be gained this way over the course of the battle), to a maximum of 6CP. Stratagems cost between 1CP and 3CP to use. The same Stratagem cannot be used to affect the same unit more than once per phase.
simulator.stratagem_per_command_phase_ca.trigger: start of own Command phase; `Battle._apply_detachment_stratagems` invoked for the army; one or more detachment stratagems in the army's detachment.stratagems tuple pass `should_fire_stratagem`
simulator.stratagem_per_command_phase_ca.effect: (approximation) the AI is permitted to fire AT MOST `Battle.DETACHMENT_STRATAGEM_CAP_PER_COMMAND_PHASE` (iter44: default 2, widened from 1) detachment-specific stratagems per army per Command phase. 10e core rules impose NO hard cap on stratagems used in a Command phase, but real-player CP economy at Strike Force CP budgets (3 start + 1/round drip, cap 6) averages 1-2 stratagems per Command phase; without this cap, CP-rich detachments (DG Virulent Vectorium, Necron Awakened Dynasty, Tau Mont'ka, Grand Coven, War Horde) would stack 3-5+ buffs at round start because every dispatcher's gate is independently green-lit when CP allows. The iter44 widening from 1 to 2 reflects real tournament play where stratagem-rich detachments stack 2-3 stratagems on alpha-strike units in a single phase (e.g. Drukhari Skysplinter Assault + Lightning-Fast Reactions + Fire and Fade, or Marines Storm of Fire + Adaptive Strategy). The cap is enforced inside `_apply_detachment_stratagems`: a counter on Army (stratagems_fired_this_command_phase) resets at the top of that method, increments inside `_fire_stratagem` while the dispatch flag is set, and short-circuits subsequent dispatcher entries via `_strat_cap_reached`. Faction-neutral: every detachment's dispatch path is gated by the same cap. Core Stratagems (Tank Shock, Heroic Intervention, Counter-Offensive, Command Re-Roll) fire on per-trigger hooks elsewhere in the round and are NOT counted toward the cap. Per-strat once-per-phase exclusion is implicit because each strat appears in the dispatcher exactly once.

simulator.conditional_invuln_save.trigger: A model whose datasheet invulnerable save is conditional on the attack type makes an invulnerable saving throw; the value differs (or is absent) depending on whether the incoming attack is melee or ranged. Examples: Aeldari Wyches (6+, improving to 4+ against melee attacks); Imperial Knight Ion Shield (a 5+ invulnerable save against ranged attacks only, none in melee).
simulator.conditional_invuln_save.effect: The defender uses its melee invulnerable save (UnitProfile.invuln_save_melee) against melee attacks and its ranged invulnerable save (invuln_save_ranged) against ranged attacks; a save that applies to one attack type only gives no invulnerable save against the other. Per-attack values are mapper-extracted from the datasheet "X+ invulnerable save against melee/ranged attacks" clauses and combined with the invuln_ranged_only override. Gated SWEG_COND_INVULN (default-on); subsumes simulator.ion_shield_ranged_only.

simulator.veterans_of_the_long_war.quoted_text: Each time a model in this unit targets an enemy unit with a melee attack, re-roll a Wound roll of 1. If that enemy unit is within range of an objective marker, you can re-roll the Wound roll instead.
simulator.veterans_of_the_long_war.trigger: A model in a Chaos Space Marines Legionaries unit makes a melee attack. The objective clause upgrades the re-roll when the target unit is within range of an objective marker.
simulator.veterans_of_the_long_war.effect: In the Fight phase the Legionaries re-roll Wound rolls of 1 (att_reroll_wound_ones); if the target is within range of any objective marker (target.on_objective), they re-roll the full failed Wound roll instead (att_reroll_all_wounds). Ranged attacks are unaffected. Applied via the override-only UnitProfile.veterans_of_the_long_war flag on chaos_space_marines_legionaries. Gated SWEG_VETERANS (default-on). Cross-checked verbatim against BSData v10.6.0 Chaos Space Marines.cat.gz ability a5ea-d708-db75-226c.

simulator.csm_despoilers.quoted_text: Each time this unit makes a Dark Pact, until the end of the phase, each time a model in this unit makes an attack, you can re-roll the Hit roll.
simulator.csm_despoilers.trigger: Chaos Terminator Squad makes a Dark Pact (at the start of the Command phase via simulator._apply_dark_pacts); fires for the remainder of that round.
simulator.csm_despoilers.effect: Unit is granted transient_reroll_all_hits for the round — every failed Hit roll may be re-rolled (att_reroll_all_hits = True in Unit.attack). Composes via OR with other att_reroll_all_hits sources. Applied via the override-only UnitProfile.csm_despoilers flag on chaos_space_marines_chaos_terminator_squad; gated SWEG_CSM_ABILITIES (default-off). Verbatim text cross-checked against BSData v10.6.0 Chaos Space Marines.cat.gz, ability id 13a2-57cd-83ff-2127.

simulator.csm_unholy_bloodshed.quoted_text: Once per battle, when this unit makes a Dark Pact, until the end of the phase, weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] ability.
simulator.csm_unholy_bloodshed.trigger: Possessed makes a Dark Pact (at the start of the Command phase via simulator._apply_dark_pacts); fires for the remainder of that round, once per battle per unit.
simulator.csm_unholy_bloodshed.effect: Unit is granted transient_devastating_wounds for the round — on a critical wound (wound roll of 6+), the attack bypasses the target's saving throws and deals mortal wounds equal to the weapon's Damage. Applied via the override-only UnitProfile.csm_unholy_bloodshed flag on chaos_space_marines_possessed; gated SWEG_CSM_ABILITIES (default-off). Once-per-battle guard tracked in Battle._csm_unholy_bloodshed_used (set of unit UIDs). Verbatim text cross-checked against BSData v10.6.0 Chaos Space Marines.cat.gz, ability id 3de3-728d-6264-1eb3.

simulator.csm_daemonic_ordnance.quoted_text: Each time this model is selected to shoot, it can use this ability. If it does, until the end of the phase, its ranged weapons have the [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] and [HAZARDOUS] abilities.
simulator.csm_daemonic_ordnance.trigger: Forgefiend (chaos_space_marines_forgefiend) is selected to shoot; fires once per shooting activation via simulator._apply_daemonic_ordnance, called from Battle._do_shoot after target selection and before attacker.attack(). Opt-in: only elected when the expected [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] offensive uplift against the chosen target exceeds the expected [HAZARDOUS] self-damage cost (0.5 expected wounds; 1.0 when below half health).
simulator.csm_daemonic_ordnance.effect: When elected: unit is granted transient_devastating_wounds (ranged weapons gain [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] — on a critical wound, bypass saves, deal mortal wounds equal to Damage) and transient_hazardous (after the ranged attack sequence, roll d6; on a 1 the unit takes 3 mortal wounds to self). Both flags are cleared per round by _clear_transient_stratagem_flags. Applied via the override-only UnitProfile.csm_daemonic_ordnance flag on chaos_space_marines_forgefiend. Verbatim text cross-checked against BSData v10.6.0 Chaos Space Marines.cat.gz, ability profile id 49a0-fe58-5293-bdc2, selectionEntry id 45b-19f6-38d2-703f.
